Give feedback

If your goal is “I want someone else to regularly plan, shoot, and turn one session into a bunch of usable videos,” I’d focus on smaller Toronto teams rather than traditional large production houses.

My shortlist

IAVA Productions — Best for a recurring content engine. They offer monthly production days designed to batch short-form content, plus podcast production and social clips. Good fit if you want to show up for a shoot and let the studio handle the rest.

Bee Video Production — Good small-studio option. Their positioning is specifically around polished, story-driven video without making you coordinate a collection of freelancers.

Barks Media — Good for ongoing brand/social content. They handle creative development through filming and editing and offer social-media content packages.

Moon Reel Media — Good boutique/creative choice. A smaller Toronto production company focused on cinematic, story-driven content, with end-to-end production.

FX Productions Canada — Good if you want more production muscle. They handle strategy, pre-production, filming and post-production, so you aren't left project-managing the shoot.

Minifridge Media — Boutique but more commercial-oriented. They cover concepting, scripting/storyboards, production and multi-format deliverables; a good choice if the videos need to look like serious advertising rather than casual social posts.

Two particularly relevant alternatives

Viterno Group is worth considering if your priority is completely done-for-you social. They explicitly offer strategy, filming, editing, posting and growth as one service, and say they have a seven-person in-house team. 
Viterno Group

Hatul Madan is interesting if you want a leaner production setup. Its core team is two people, and its social package currently starts at $2,700 + HST for up to four hours of filming and up to six edited short-form videos. 
Hatul Madan
+1

What I'd ask for

Rather than asking, “How much is a video?”, I'd tell these studios:

“I want one half-day or full-day shoot every month that gives me 8–20 pieces of social content. I don't want to write every script, edit anything, or manage the production. Can you handle the ideas, filming, editing and delivery?”

That immediately separates the true done-for-you content partners from studios that mainly sell one-off videos.

If I were narrowing this to 3 companies for a Toronto small-business owner, I'd start with IAVA, Barks Media, and Viterno for ongoing content, with Hatul Madan as the lower-overhead option.
